newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Asia aluminium premium surge seen fading soon.
newsitem.headline: Asia aluminium premium surge seen fading soon.

text.p: A surge in aluminium ingot spot premiums to Asia may be short-lived as strong demand in the United States starts to recede, metals dealer said on Friday.

Spot premiums for aluminium from Australia, Russia, India and other countries have jumped to to as high as US$100 a tonne over the London Metal Exchange (LME) benchmark price in Singapore and Japan on the back of higher premiums quoted in the U.S., the metals dealers said.
Quotations for deliveries starting in August suggest a return to more normal premium levels of around US$55-$70 a tonne, the dealers said.

"It's really only for July and possibly early August, with the premiums for third quarter aluminium under frame (long term) contracts from the big Australian producers much lower," a trader in Sydney said. "The spot stuff is more like US$90 to $100."
"U.S. spot premiums of as much as six to eight cents a pound (US132-$176 a tonne) since April has provided little incentive to export metal," another dealer said.
"That's just kept a lot material on shore in the U.S., which drives the premiums to Japan up," the trader said.
Declining aluminium stocks in the LME's Singapore warehouse were also underpinning premiums, traders said.
LME aluminium stocks in Singapore declined to 8,300 tonnes on Thursday from 11,275 tonnes at the beginning of June.
Australian aluminium production is forecast to rise 11.7 percent to 1.56 million tonnes in 1997/98 (July/June), the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said this week.
